name: Vandiyur Mariamman Temple
significance: A Mariamman temple on the banks of the Vaigai about 3 km from the Meenakshi Amman Temple, raised under the Madurai Nayaks. Its large tank, the Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam, is fed by underground channels from the river and hosts the float festival on Thaipusam.

name: Valiyakoikkal Temple
significance: The shrine inside the Pandalam Palace grounds that serves as the family temple of the Pandalam royal family, now administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board. The annual Thiruvabharanam procession carrying Ayyappan's ornaments to Sabarimala for Makaravilakku sets out from here.

name: Uthirakosamangai Mangaleswarar Temple
significance: A roughly 20-acre Shiva temple with a seven-tiered rajagopuram, sung by the 9th-century saint Manickavasagar in the Thiruvasakam and prominent under Pandya rule. It is known for an unusual six-foot emerald image of Nataraja and is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared in Ravana's palace as a small child, and when he was lifted a fireball rose from the temple tank, at which 999 of the thousand rishis present immolated themselves while the last survived to preserve the sacred texts.

name: Trikkur Mahadeva Temple
significance: A rock-cut Shiva temple set inside a natural cave about 30 feet long on a hillock in Trikkur, with its mukha mandapa carved from the living rock. It has been a protected monument under the Kerala Department of Archaeology since 1966 and is looked after by the Paliyam Trust and a local protection committee.
story: The large Shivalinga is believed to have been consecrated by Agni, who is said to worship Shiva here perpetually, which is why the image is never taken outside in procession during the rains.

name: Vamana Temple, Khajuraho
significance: An eastern-group Khajuraho temple raised by the Chandela rulers between about 1050 and 1075 CE, comprising a sanctum, vestibule, maha-mandapa with lateral transepts and an entrance porch. It stands roughly 200 m north-east of the Brahma Temple and forms part of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Unao Balaji Sun Temple
deity: Surya (the Sun God, worshipped here as Balaji)
significance: A sun temple at Unao, about 17 km from both Datia and Jhansi, whose shrine is engraved with twenty-one triangles taken to represent the twenty-one phases of the Sun, the image standing on a brick platform faced with black plates. Its main priesthood is hereditary in the Kachhi Kushwaha Kshatriya community, and pilgrims bathe for skin ailments in the sulphurous water of the nearby Pahuj river.
story: A cow belonging to a Kushwaha Kshatriya villager is said to have poured out her milk at one spot, where a statue of the Sun God was then found; the king of Datia built the temple there and made the cowherd's community its hereditary priests.

name: Valisvara Temple, Thiruvalisvaram
significance: An early 10th-century Chola foundation in Tirunelveli district, credited to Rajaraja Chola I and rated among the finest surviving examples of Chola temple architecture. Its sculpture, including a Chandesanugrahamurti and an Ardhanarishvara on the vimana, was singled out by the historian K. A. Nilakanta Sastri as unsurpassed workmanship.

name: Ucchi Pillayar Temple, Rockfort
significance: A shrine to Ganesha on the summit of the Rockfort at Tiruchirappalli, reached by steps cut into the rock, whose caves were first excavated by the Pallavas in the 7th century and whose temples were completed by the Nayaks of Madurai under the Vijayanagara Empire. The site is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India and looks out over Trichy, Srirangam and the rivers below.
story: Ganesha is said to have taken the form of a Brahmin boy and set down the image of Ranganatha that Vibhishana was carrying to Lanka, so that it stayed at Srirangam.

name: Valayanad Devi Temple
significance: A north-facing goddess temple with four gopurams that served as the family shrine of the medieval Zamorins of Kozhikode. Worship follows the Saktheya tradition under Pidarar Brahmin priests, with hereditary rights held by five Moosad families, and the annual festival runs seven days from Karthika in Makaram.
story: The Zamorin is said to have done penance until Bhagavathy appeared and agreed to follow him to his kingdom; when he looked back on the way she halted and flung her bangle, which spun for a week before falling where the temple now stands.

name: Upper Bagh Devi Temple
deity: Bagh Devi (Byaghra Devi), a form of Shakti
significance: A hilltop Shakti shrine at Kulada in Ganjam district, about 8 km from Bhanjanagar, long associated with the Odia poet Upendra Bhanja. A second shrine was later built at the foot of the hill so that pilgrims unable to climb could worship.
story: Local tradition holds that three sisters divided the region by hurling vessels and a temple was raised wherever one fell, the third having sunk from sight, and that the goddess appeared to Upendra Bhanja in a dream telling him to build the shrines.

name: Trilokpur Mahamaya Bala Sundari Temple
deity: Bhagwati Tripur Mahamaya Bala Sundari (Durga in her child form)
significance: A marble temple about 24 km south-west of Nahan, begun in 1570 and dedicated in 1573 by the ruler of Sirmour using artisans brought from Jaipur, and later renovated by Maharaja Fateh Prakash in 1823 and Maharaja Raghubir Prakash in 1851. It is run by a temple trust headed by the Deputy Commissioner of Sirmaur and draws several million pilgrims a year.
story: A sacred stone is said to have appeared in a salt merchant's sack in 1570 after the goddess came to Ram Dass in a dream, and the temple was raised where she had shown herself.

name: Varaha Temple, Khajuraho
deity: Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu
significance: A sandstone pavilion with a pyramidal roof on a high plinth in the Western Group at Khajuraho, built by the Chandela rulers around 900-925 CE. It shelters a monolithic boar image 2.6 m long and 1.7 m high covered in carved figures, including a Saraswati between the snout and mouth, and forms part of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments inscribed by UNESCO in 1986.
story: Vishnu is said to have taken the form of a boar and fought Hiranyaksha for a thousand years before lifting the earth goddess Bhudevi out of the cosmic ocean and setting her back in her place.

name: Velleeswarar Temple, Mylapore
significance: A roughly two-acre south-facing Shiva temple with a five-tier vimana on South Mada Street in Mylapore, close to the Kapaleeswarar Temple. It is counted among the seven Sapta Sthana Shiva temples of Mylapore and holds shrines to Ganesha, Kamakshi, the seven mother goddesses, Durga, Kartikeya, Bhairava and the Navagrahas.
story: Shukra, blinded by a blade of darbha grass from Vamana, is said to have meditated on Shiva at this spot and recovered his sight, which is why devotees pray here for eyesight.

name: Sheetala Chaukiya Dham
significance: A goddess temple near Jaunpur that takes the name Chaukiya from the raised platform on which the deity was first installed; its founding is credited to the Ahir ruler Heerchand Yadav, while some historians attribute it to the Bhars. It is among the busiest shrines of the district and has been the subject of a state tourism modernisation project.
story: Durga is said to have taken birth as Katyayani and then as Shitala Devi, carrying the implements of healing, to undo the fevers and diseases spread by the demon Jvarasura.

name: Thamaramkulangara Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
significance: A Dharma Sastha temple built in the Kerala architectural tradition at Tripunithura, on the eastern edge of Kochi. Its founding date is not recorded, and the temple appears in the 2019 survey Pilgrimage to Temple Heritage.

name: Binsar Mahadev Temple
significance: A rock temple in the Chauthan region of Pauri Garhwal, dated to the 9th or 10th century and held to have been raised by Maharaja Prithu in memory of his father Bindu. The original structure with its rock-cut images was pulled down in October 2017 to make way for a new building; an annual fair is still held here on Vaikuntha Chaturdashi.
story: Villagers hold that the Pandavas built the temple in a single night during their exile, or else that the divine architect Vishwakarma raised it.

name: Shri Kali Devi Temple, Patiala
significance: A Kali temple opposite the Baradari Gardens in Patiala, begun in 1936 and completed in 1938 by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh, who had the six-foot images of Maa Kali and the Paawan Jyot brought from Bengal. The goddess is kept as a kul devi by many families and the shrine draws large crowds through the Navratras.

name: Somanatha Pashana Lingeswarar Temple, Timiri
significance: A modern Shiva temple in the village of Timiri in Vellore district, completed in 1985. It takes its name from its presiding lingam, Somanatha Pashana Lingeswarar.

name: Bhutanatha Group of Temples, Badami
style: Dravida and Early Chalukya; Nagara phamsana
significance: Two clusters of Shiva temples on the east bank of Agastya lake at Badami: the main Bhutanatha group of the 7th-8th centuries under the Badami Chalukyas, whose principal shrine has a gudha-mandapa on four pillars beneath a three-storeyed superstructure, and the Mallikarjuna group of the 11th-12th centuries built under the Kalyani Chalukyas. A late 9th-century inscription naming Sridharbuteswara shows the site was still in use between the two building phases, and a smaller northern shrine is thought to have been Vaishnava before it passed to Lingayat worship.
